etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Ancient Greek αὐστηρός (austērós, “bitter, harsh, astringent”), having the specific meaning “making the tongue dry” (originally used of fruits, wines), related to αὔω (aúō, “to singe”), αὖος (aûos, “dry”).
senses: Grim or severe in manner or appearance.
Lacking decoration; trivial; not extravagant or gaudy.
